sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the worlds were created from the light of the line (kav), not from the light before the tzimtzum, and that the line's qualities of being a defined light with up and down parallel the concealment and limitation of the world, which is called Mitzrayim.

translations.translation: And he continues in the maamar,
that the coming into being of the worlds is from the light of the line (kav).
For from the light that preceded the tzimtzum (constriction), it was impossible for the worlds to come into being
(as they are now),
because the worlds are in the category of above and below
[for this is the definition of "world" (olam) as place,
for the concept of place in spirituality is above and below],
and the light before the tzimtzum had no beginning, end, above, or below.
And also,
because the totality of the light before the tzimtzum is light that is included in His Essence (Atzmus),
and light that is included in the Luminary (Maor) is in a state of ultimate nullification, to the point that it is not even called by the name "light" at all,
and consequently it cannot be a source for the worlds,
for in order to be a source for something, the source must have some form of existence.
And specifically through the light of the line (kav),
which, by being drawn down through the tzimtzum, is in the category of existence of light,
and it has above and below,
specifically through it does the coming into being of the worlds occur.
And it can be said,
that these two aspects in the line are analogous to the two aspects mentioned above in the world.
For the above and below in the line is analogous to the boundary of the world,
and that the line is an existence of light
(which is not in a state of ultimate nullification)
is analogous to the concealment and hiding of the world
(the cause of the yeshus (selfhood) within it).
And based on the above, that the worlds are called by the name "Mitzrayim" because they are in the category of constriction (meitzar) and concealment
(these two aspects),
it can be said,
that the line is also included in the category of Mitzrayim,
and the true essence of the concept of Yetzias Mitzrayim (the Exodus from Egypt),
the departure from all constrictions and limitations,
is through the revelation of the Essence (Atzmus) of the Ein Sof that preceded the tzimtzum.
And this is that in the future redemption there will be the perfection of Yetzias Mitzrayim
(the departure from all constrictions and limitations),
for then there will be a revelation of the light that preceded the tzimtzum,
and within this itself—a revelation of the light that is beyond and above (b'li gvul) the light that relates to the worlds,
and even to the revelation of the Essence (Atzmus).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section states that in the future, the departure from all limitations will apply to all matters—the world, the Torah, and the revelation of G-dliness—and that this will be achieved specifically through a new form of service at the end of the exile.

translations.translation: And behold, that in the future to come there will be the departure from all constrictions and limitations,
this applies to all matters.
For all matters of the future to come will be incomparable relative to how they are now.
Both regarding the world,
for then there will be new heavens and a new earth
(a new world),
and regarding the Torah
[through which the world was created,
"He looked into the Torah and created the world"],
for in the future to come there will be "a new Torah from Me shall go forth,"
and regarding the drawing down and revelation of G-dliness,
for the revelation of G-dliness that will be in the future to come is a new revelation, incomparably higher than the revelation of the present,
for all present revelations are from the externality of Atik, and in the future to come there will be the revelation of the innerness of Atik.
And this is that the future redemption will be primarily through the service (avodah) at the conclusion of the time of exile,
for since all matters of the future to come will be new matters,
therefore,
also the service through which these matters are drawn down must be a new service,
as will be explained below.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contrasts the service of the era of the Holy Temple, which was within reason and intellect, with the service in the generation of the heels of Moshiach, which is a service of self-sacrifice beyond measure, stemming from the innerness of the soul.

translations.translation: And the explanation is,
that in the time of the Holy Temple,
when there was a revelation of G-dliness,
"ten miracles were performed for our forefathers in the Holy Temple,"
miracles that were visible to physical sight, to the extent that some of them were also seen by the ignorant,
the service of fulfilling the Torah and mitzvos was according to reason and intellect.
And even though then too there was the commandment
"And you shall love... with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might,"
nevertheless,
since they then saw a tangible revelation of G-dliness,
even in the self-sacrifice (mesiras nefesh) that existed then,
there was measurement and limitation of reason and intellect.
And likewise in the time of exile, when the darkness was not so intense.
However, in the generation of the heels of Moshiach (ikvesa d'meshicha),
when each day the darkness intensifies,
and there are many trials,
and particularly the trial of "not being ashamed before those who mock,"
and all the more so when the mockers are lowly and empty people,
which is very difficult to bear,
behold, that one stands in these trials,
this is a service of self-sacrifice (mesiras nefesh) that is above measurement and limitation.
And this is that the service in the generation of the heels of Moshiach,
and in this very generation—at the conclusion of the time of exile,
is loftier
(in this aspect)
than the services that were until now,
and in an incomparable manner,
to the point that it is a new service,
for the matters of service of previous generations
had some connection to reason and intellect
(measurement and limitation of revealed faculties),
whereas the service at the conclusion of the time of exile is the service of self-sacrifice (mesiras nefesh) that stems from the innerness of the soul.
